workflowRecommendation: Sequential, one implementer. Tasks 1 and 2 are independent of each other and of the rest; Tasks 3-4 must land in one commit (adding the identity check to probe breaks every existing liveness test until the fixtures carry identity). TDD per task: write the failing test, run only that file, implement, re-run. Commit with `jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" describe -m "<msg>" && jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" new` after each task's file-scoped tests pass; run the daemon package suite, tsc, and biome once at the end (Task 6).
spec: Dispatch issue LEGION-27 primary document (dispatch_doc_read issue=LEGION-27). Its Design, Errors, Testing, Rejected sections are the contract; this plan argues from it. Settled and not to be re-decided: identity = pane root pid + /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 start ticks recorded at launch; single-issue scope; tmux runtime otherwise unchanged (LEGION-19 restructures later).
goal: A tmux pane id is never taken as proof of the process a locator recorded. Every locator (tree root, worker, controller) records the pane's root pid and that process's start ticks at launch; every liveness probe, every daemon-issued kill-pane, and every window reuse first verifies the pane still runs exactly that process.
globalConstraints: Biome: double quotes, semicolons, ES5 trailing commas, 100-char width. `node:` prefix for builtins, `type` imports. No barrel files. Interfaces for object shapes, types for unions.

Tests: bun:test, co-located `__tests__/`. Run single files: `cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && bun test packages/daemon/src/daemon/__tests__/<file>`. Never run the repo-wide suite mid-task; Task 6 runs the daemon package once.
jj, not git. Every shell command begins `cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" &&`; every jj command uses `-R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE"`. Never `jj abandon`, never `jj edit @-`.
Comments describe current behaviour, not history. Delete code the change obsoletes (the tmuxPaneId backfill, tmux.windowAlive, tmux.firstPaneId); no shims or aliases.
Keep the tmux runtime otherwise unchanged: no Runtime boundary, no change to reconnectWorkers' socket probe, no change to reconcileTmuxWindows' logic (doc comment only).
The working copy already contains a `.omp/config.yml` added by workspace provisioning. Leave it alone; commit only your own files.

decisions.decision: Bump the state version 23 -> 24 with a pure no-op `migrateV23State`.
decisions.why: The file's own convention bumps for every schema-shape change even when fields are optional (v14->v15 `completed`, v21->v22 `approvalStatusPending`), and `migrateV19State`'s comment records the cost of once skipping a bump. The bump also makes `loadState` write `state.json.v23.bak` on first load, preserving the pre-identity state file for an operator diffing an incident. The migration leaves legacy locators identity-less on purpose (spec Rejected: clearing them strands roots).

decisions.decision: One helper `verifyPaneProcess(locator): Promise<PaneVerdict>` returning a discriminated verdict rather than a boolean.
decisions.why: Spec requires `stopProcess` to log both identities on a mismatch; a boolean would force a second tmux/proc read for the log. Boolean-only callers (`probedWindowId`, the watchdog closure) read `.verified`.

decisions.decision: Watchdog dep is `paneProcessVerified(locator: WorkerLocator): Promise<boolean>`, replacing (not sitting beside) `isOmpPane` and `tmux` in `WorkerBootWatchdogDeps`.
decisions.why: `probeAlive` was the watchdog's only user of both; delegating its pane branch leaves them dead. The spec's 'injected beside isOmpPane' names the mechanism (injection); clean cutover forbids leaving dead deps. `isOmpPane` itself stays in processes.ts as the last step of `verifyPaneProcess`.

decisions.decision: Identity is recorded inside `launchShimmedProcess` (covers spawnTree and launchWorker, which both call it) and inside `spawnController`.
decisions.why: `spawnTree` never calls tmux itself; the spec's naming of spawnTree/launchShimmedProcess/spawnController maps to these two code sites.

decisions.decision: An unreadable `/proc/<pid>/stat` right after tmux reported a pane throws from `recordedPaneIdentity`; the throw rides the existing launch-failure paths (`launchWorker`'s catch -> launchFailures; `spawnRoot`'s catch -> rollback + launchFailures; `spawnController`'s rejection -> `ensureController` rejects as for any spawn failure). A read failure at probe time is `stat-unreadable` -> not verified; a *malformed* stat line throws from the parser at both sites (a bug, never 'dead').
decisions.why: Spec Errors rows 3 and 5. A pid tmux just reported whose /proc entry is gone means the process already exited: there is no orphan to kill (the pane closes itself; a fresh window whose sole pane died vanishes, so the issue-window map's stale id is dropped by the next probedWindowId). Distinguishing fs errors from parse errors keeps 'no silent fallbacks': a wrong field index must crash loud, not resurrect every root.

decisions.decision: `stopProcess` gates kill-pane on the full `verifyPaneProcess` verdict (including `isOmpPane`), returning normally on any non-verified verdict so callers clear the locator exactly as they do for PANE_GONE_STDERR today; `pane-gone` is silent, every other reason logs both identities.
decisions.why: Spec Errors row 4 and acceptance 5. One rule ('kill iff it is our process') is what a maintainer can hold. A `not-omp` verdict cannot occur for a pane we launched (its shim command line always contains `omp`). A legacy identity-less locator whose graceful stop times out is therefore never killed by the daemon; once its locator clears, its pane is an unrecorded shim pane that `reconcileTmuxWindows` reaps after the grace period.

decisions.decision: Delete the `tmuxPaneId` backfill blocks in `probe`/`controllerAlive`, and `tmux.firstPaneId` + `tmux.windowAlive`.
decisions.why: A locator without a pane id has no identity, so it never verifies and is retired/resurrected on first probe onto a fully-recorded locator: the backfill is unreachable. `windowAlive`'s only caller was `probedWindowId`, which now verifies recorded panes instead. `reconcileTmuxWindows`' exemption for pane-id-less locators stays (its comment is rewritten to name the new mechanism by which it shrinks).

decisions.decision: Do NOT add `panePid`/`paneStartTicks` to the redacted `GET /legion/v1/state` projection (`api/state.ts`).
decisions.why: That response is a strict allowlist validated against `LegionDaemonApi.State.response` in `@legion/contracts`; extending it is a contracts change outside the spec's change set. `state.json` carries the identity for diagnosis.

nonGoals: No Runtime abstraction, no Kubernetes/`--connect` shim changes (LEGION-19).
No change to `reconnectWorkers`' socket-first probe; identity reaches an unconfirmed boot via the watchdog it re-arms and a root via the registration deadline / resync probe (spec Design).
No smoke-rig (`scripts/smoke`) work; the tester owns the acceptance-3 throwaway-tmux driver. Task 6 has a two-minute implementer smoke only.

tasks.title: Package-level verification and a two-minute real-tmux smoke

steps.run: cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && bunx biome check packages/daemon/src && bunx tsc --noEmit -p packages/daemon && (cd packages/daemon && bun test)

steps.step: Throwaway smoke on a private throwaway tmux server (never the deployment's `legion-<project>` socket). Not committed. Shows the recorded identity flipping when the server is recreated and the parser reading a real stat line.
steps.run:
cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && S=legion-smoke-$RANDOM && \
tmux -L "$S" new-session -d -s smoke 'sleep 600' && \
REPORT=$(tmux -L "$S" list-panes -t smoke -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_pid}') && echo "before: $REPORT" && \
PID=${REPORT#* } && STAT=$(cat /proc/$PID/stat) && \
bun -e 'import { parseProcStatStartTicks } from "./packages/daemon/src/daemon/proc-stat.ts"; console.log("start ticks:", parseProcStatStartTicks(process.argv[1]))' "$STAT" && \
tmux -L "$S" kill-server && \
tmux -L "$S" new-session -d -s smoke 'sleep 600' && \
echo "after:  $(tmux -L "$S" list-panes -t smoke -F '#{pane_id} #{pane_pid}')" && \
tmux -L "$S" kill-server
steps.expect: `before` and `after` print the same pane id (`%0`) with different pids; `start ticks:` prints a positive integer. Record both lines in `.legion/implement.json` as the smoke evidence; the tester's acceptance-3 driver builds on this.

tasks.acceptance: biome, tsc, and the daemon package suite green; smoke output recorded.

concerns: Many existing tests launch panes with pid `1000${n}` (e.g. ~4189) or `67890` (split) and then answer `list-panes` with `livePanes` defaults (12345). With identity recorded at launch these now read as pid-mismatch -> dead. Rule (a) in Task 4 covers it; budget most of the sweep time there.

processes.test.ts is ~9900 lines with ~180 tests seeding identity-less locators; the Task 4 sweep is mechanical but wide. Rule (a) covers nearly all; do not restructure the fixture beyond `procStat`/`paneIdentity`/default `readProcessStat`.

T2's watchdog-interval observation relies on the same fake-clock wiring as the existing test at ~3527; if `flushEventLoopUntil` on the re-arm log proves brittle, observe the re-arm via `state.roles[liveToken].locator` still set after the interval AND the retire log's absence — never by making the live claim confirmed, which would skip the interval the spec's test names.

After a server recreate, `rewriteIssueWindowId` (existing behaviour) repoints stale locators' `tmuxWindowId` to the fresh window while their `tmuxPaneId`/identity stay stale; identity still catches them on the next probe. `reconcileTmuxWindows`' knownPanes set will contain those stale pane ids until they clear — a pre-existing narrowing hazard, unchanged here.
The `/state` API response does not expose identity (strict contract allowlist). If the tester wants to observe recorded identity, `cat <state_dir>/state.json` is the surface.
